title: Office
description: A post held by one person after another — a crown, a presidency, a party's general secretaryship, a command. It is a record and not code, so a sultanate, a doge or a chief is added by writing a file (plan decision 1). `of` is the actor whose office it is; which kind of actor that may be is decided by the category, in a table in src/vocab.js that rule 26 checks. Who held it and when is a tenure, never a field here.

sources.description: An office is a fact about how an actor is arranged rather than an argument about the world, so rule 6 exempts it as it exempts a place: the list is written empty. The tenures that say who held it each cite at least one source.

of.description: The actor whose office this is — the state, the party, the body. Which kind of actor may stand here is decided by the category (rule 26).

title.description: What the post is called, as its own actor calls it: "King of Portugal", "Prime Minister", "Secretary-General".

category.description: What kind of post it is. Closed, and small on purpose: it decides which kind of actor may stand at `of`, and it is what an Offices grouping and an office strip are drawn by. A category nobody has decided about is reported in STATUS.md, never replaced by `other`.

when.description: How long the office itself existed, or null where the atlas asserts only that it exists and what its tenures were. Null is not a gap to be filled with a guess: dating the Portuguese crown against an actor record that begins in 1886 would be an invented claim (amendment A13). Rule 26's overlap check is skipped where this is null.

summary.description: Optional, and written by a person when it is there: what the post is, in their own words.
